File 01  How it works

What if you could learn robotics through an RPG quest?

That was the first question we asked when we fell in love with space tech. We couldn’t find a programme like that, so we built one. Students team up, build a real machine and solve a space mystery along the way.

You build

A real machine.

Design, 3D-print, wire and program a working robot with your team. Real parts, real problems to fix.

You investigate

A space mystery.

A past mission failed. Collect clues, test your ideas and find out what really happened.

01

Get the mission

Every crew gets a story, a goal and a deadline.

02

Pick your role

Engineer, programmer, electronics, 3D designer or team lead.

03

Build it

Turn ideas into a working machine, step by step, with mentors next to you.

04

Crack the case

Gather clues and test every theory on real hardware.

05

Present it

Show what you built and what you found, and earn your certificate.

File 02  Why we exist

We fell in love with space.School almost talked us out of it

Most of us met rockets and robots through textbooks: formulas, definitions, exams. Interesting, but miles away from anything you could hold. It only clicked when we started building, and breaking, real hardware with a team around us.

That’s what Space Lumen Academy is for. We put students inside a mission: a crew, a deadline, a machine to build and a mystery to solve. CAD, electronics and code stop being school subjects. They’re the tools you grab because the rover won’t drive without them.

No back row! It’s time for everyone to build something.

Missions

Intensive, story-driven builds

Each programme runs as a mission with a brief, a crew structure, a timeline and a final defence.

Academy

Skills taught at the point of need

3D modelling, electronics, firmware, payload science and project management, learned while building.

Community

A crew that stays together

Graduates return as assistants, mentors and the people who design the next mission.

Lineage  Where we come from

Raised on the golden age of science fiction.

Asimov showed us that science can be a story. Clarke, that the impossible is the next engineering problem. Herbert, Bradbury, Lem and the Strugatsky brothers, that the future is something people build and argue about.

We teach the way those books made us feel: curious, a little uneasy, and ready to build.

Offline, online, and built for partners.

The same mission format, delivered in the room, across cities, or around a partner’s own audience.

OfflineMission 01 complete

In-person missions

A one-month intensive in Tashkent. A small crew builds a working prototype with mentors at the table, from first sketch to final defence.

Online RPG missions

A full role-playing game online. You play yourself as a scientist on a simulated space mission: plan, explore, solve problems and reach shared goals with your crew. It grows more than tech skills: creativity, writing, teamwork and critical thinking.

File 04  Case file LUM-001Mission complete

Mission 01:
Moonrover.

Tashkent · 10 Aug – 2 Sep 2026 · Free for participants

The crew was appointed to an inquiry board. A lunar rover had landed at the Moon’s south pole and gone silent after its first drive. Their task: build its successor from the same design, then find out what stopped the first one. Four weeks later they had a six-wheel rover with a working robotic arm.

A working rover

Six wheels, rocker suspension, 3D-printed body, sensors, radio link and a robotic arm.

Real mission roles

Each participant owned a subsystem, with leads in engineering, programming, electronics and 3D.

An investigation

Evidence requests, test logs and a causal chain defended in front of a panel.

Certificates by role

Awarded for the subsystem each participant built and led.
